title: Week 35 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “policy instrument”?
options: A tradition holding that moral principles can be discovered through reason and apply beyond enacted rules.
A tax, subsidy, rule, service, information requirement, public investment, legal right, or other mechanism used to pursue a goal.
A legislature’s grant of authority to an executive agency or official.
A public guarantee protecting eligible deposits up to legal limits.
questions.explanation: Policy instrument means a tax, subsidy, rule, service, information requirement, public investment, legal right, or other mechanism used to pursue a goal.
choices: A tradition holding that moral principles can be discovered through reason and apply beyond enacted rules.
A tax, subsidy, rule, service, information requirement, public investment, legal right, or other mechanism used to pursue a goal.
A legislature’s grant of authority to an executive agency or official.
A public guarantee protecting eligible deposits up to legal limits.

A political system concentrating power and limiting meaningful competition, accountability, and civil liberties.
Examination of how costs, benefits, risks, and opportunities differ across groups.
A significant, broad decline in economic activity lasting more than a brief fluctuation.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 35 inquiry?
options: A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student states the decision rule, cites evidence, identifies jurisdiction and implementation, and explains uncertainty and distribution.
questions.explanation: A student states the decision rule, cites evidence, identifies jurisdiction and implementation, and explains uncertainty and distribution.
